dedupe_keys.name: rotated horizontal to vertical spectral ratios on ambient noise hvnsr rot recordings of stations of the 6n network during the activities of the emersito ingv emergency group in ancona italy following the 2022 mw 5 5 costa marchigiana pesarese earthquake

description: Italy’s Istituto Nazionale di Geofisica e Vulcanologia publishes rotated horizontal-to-vertical spectral ratios derived from ambient noise at the temporary Ancona 6N stations. The stations were deployed for roughly four months after the November 2022 Adriatic earthquake. Each public text file contains three comma-separated columns: frequency in hertz, rotation angle of the horizontal components and the mean noise spectral ratio. Zenodo distributes the files free under CC-BY-4.0. The rotation dimension supports investigation of directional site response, but ambient-noise excitation is not equivalent to strong earthquake shaking. That limitation and the finite observation period matter when selecting amplification assumptions. The tables can help constrain directional ground-response simulations for buildings in Ancona. They complement the corresponding unrotated noise ratios and earthquake-based rotated ratios from the same network. The original noise waveforms are a separate resource; no processing or structural analysis was performed. Coverage is limited to Ancona.
